summary:
ORBIT X: Interactive Space Mission Design & Simulation Game

ORBIT X is an interactive educational website that I independently developed to make space mission design engaging, accessible, and enjoyable for students. Inspired by the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, I created this project to transform complex aerospace engineering concepts into an immersive, hands-on learning experience that goes beyond traditional textbook education.

Through ORBIT X, users can explore planetary destinations, choose difficulty levels, design spacecraft, select scientific instruments, manage limited mission resources, and simulate space missions. Each decision helps users understand the engineering challenges and trade-offs involved in planning a successful space mission.

My primary intention is to encourage students to learn through exploration, experimentation, and problem-solving rather than simply memorising scientific concepts. By combining education with interactive gameplay, I aim to make space science more approachable while developing curiosity, creativity, and critical thinking.

I believe learning about space should not just be theoretical; it should be an experience where students can imagine, design, experiment, and explore.
details: My Space Mission is a browser-based interactive aerospace and planetary science simulation game engineered to immerse learners in the end-to-end systems engineering lifecycle of a spaceflight mission. Rather than treating mission planning as isolated textbook theory, the simulation guides users through an integrated operational workflow—spanning Home, Destination, Difficulty, Mission Control, Design Lab, Fitness, Launch, Challenges, Analysis, and Rules & Science. Users begin from a guided SYSTEM READY entry state (Start Your Mission) supported by onboarding and reference modules (How to Play, Mission Guide, NASA Research Library, and About the Project), then select from 9 distinct mission profiles formed by pairing three target regimes (Earth Orbit, The Moon, and Mars) with three difficulty tiers (Beginner/Youth, Intermediate, and Advanced). Inside the Design Lab, players synthesize a spacecraft architecture and scientific payload suite while negotiating coupled engineering trade-offs, validate readiness through pre-flight Fitness diagnostics, execute Launch, mitigate stochastic or environmental Challenges, and inspect a decision-driven Analysis of mission performance. Learners gain substantial pedagogical and practical benefits from this architecture. Zero-installation, zero-login browser execution lowers entry barriers for students and youth audiences, while immediate causal feedback turns abstract astrodynamics, telemetry, and hardware constraints into tangible experiential learning. By requiring players to reconcile competing subsystem demands before liftoff, the experience cultivates systems thinking, quantitative resource allocation, risk literacy, and sustained STEM engagement. Technically, Orbit X was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for interactive state management, UI orchestration, and real-time simulation logic, authored and tested in a live browser-based web development environment (CodePen) with AI-assisted ideation, structuring, and iteration (Gemini and super intelligence) across standard mobile and desktop hardware and modern web browsers. Creatively, Orbit X unifies spacecraft architecture, pre-launch verification, flight execution, and post-mission evaluation into a single cohesive feedback loop where downstream outcomes are governed by upstream design choices. Beyond core gameplay mechanics, the design incorporates layered atmospheric visuals (such as a starfield canvas, nebula layer, and planetary backdrop), live mission status indicators (including destination status, difficulty status, and spacecraft health telemetry)
